claims.text: A machine-learning approach such as a neural-network potential can predict high-temperature thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy materials.
The proposed approach can improve determination of the transition temperature.
The proposed approach can improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy.
The proposed approach can improve determination of the volume change at the transition.
The proposed approach can improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
The neural-network potential would learn thermodynamic behavior from a dataset of ab initio calculations.
Learning from ab initio calculations would enable efficient prediction of thermodynamic properties such as Gibbs energies.
The proposed approach would permit treatment of both solid and fluid phases around the transition.
The proposed approach would remain practical across relevant compositions and temperatures.
The approach would be more accurate than existing experimental and computational baselines.
The approach would be more efficient than DFT free-energy studies and TOR-TILD.
The approach is limited to high-entropy materials at high temperatures.
Training the proposed approach requires a large dataset of ab initio calculations.
A comparison against existing experimental and computational methods across a set of high-entropy materials can test the proposed performance improvement.
Failure to improve both accuracy and efficiency relative to existing methods would falsify the hypothesis.
